questions.q: Where did Solomon put the things which David had dedicated to God?
questions.a: Solomon put all the things including the silver, gold, and all the furnishings, into the storerooms of the house of God.

questions.q: What did Solomon decide to do next?
questions.a: Solomon assembled the leaders of Israel to bring up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh from the city of David.

questions.q: What did King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel do when the Levites brought up the ark of the covenant?
questions.a: King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel came together sacrificing many sheep and oxen.

questions.q: Where did the priests place the ark of the covenant of Yahweh?
questions.a: The priests placed the ark of the covenant of Yahweh in the most holy place under the wings of the cherubim.

questions.q: What items were in the ark of the covenant?
questions.a: There was nothing in the ark of the covenant except the two tablets that Moses had put there at Horeb.

questions.q: What did all the Levites do after the priests came out of the holy place?
questions.a: The Levites, who were clothed in fine linen, stood at the east end of the altar playing cymbals, harps, and lyres.

questions.q: How did the trumpeters and singers praise Yahweh?
questions.a: The trumpeters and singers made music together, singing, “For he is good, for his covenant loyalty endures forever.”

questions.q: Why were the priests unable to stand in order to serve?
questions.a: The priests could not stand because the cloud, which was the glory of Yahweh, filled Yahweh’s house.

commentary.text: The ark placed in the temple.

Verses 1–10 The ark was a type of Christ, and, as such, a token of the presence of God. That gracious promise, Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world, does, in effect, bring the ark into our religious assemblies, if we by faith and prayer plead that promise; and this we should be most earnest for. When Christ is formed in a soul, the law written in the heart, the ark of the covenant settled there, so that it becomes the temple of the Holy Ghost, there is true satisfaction in that soul.

God took possession of the temple; he filled it with a cloud. Thus he signified his acceptance of this temple, to be the same to him that the tabernacle of Moses was, and assured his people that he would be the same in it. Would we have God dwell in our hearts, we must leave room for him; every thing else must give way. The Word was made flesh; and when he comes to his temple, like a refiner's fire, who may abide the day of his coming? May he prepare us for that day.
